label: Freshservice
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Freshservice IT service management

tools.name: FindKnownCause
tools.description:
Find the change or known problem that already explains a wave of tickets about one system.

Searches recent changes and tracked problems together and ranks them as one
most-recent-first list, so a caller asking "what explains this" makes one
call instead of two and does not have to merge the answers itself. Changes
and problems stay in their own fields of the response, since a change that
went out and a problem being tracked call for different next steps.

Give change_id or problem_id on its own to fetch that one record with its
full description; combining either with the other, or with any filter, is
rejected rather than silently resolved one way or the other.

A filtered search covers a bounded, most-recent working set rather than the
entire history, so an empty result is not proof that no such change or
problem exists; the response states how far the scan actually reached.

parameters.name: about
parameters.description: A free-text term naming the affected system, matched case-insensitively against each change's and problem's subject and description. Every whitespace-separated word must appear in the same field, in any order, so 'vpn gateway' and 'gateway vpn' match the same records and a word that appears nowhere excludes the record. Defaults to empty, which returns recent causes unnarrowed.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only include causes in this status. Changes use open, planning, approval, pending_release, pending_review, or closed; problems use open, change_requested, or closed. A status only one of the two defines narrows the search to that kind. A tenant-customized status's numeric code applies to both. Defaults to empty, which applies no status filter.

parameters.name: change_id
parameters.description: The internal id of one change to fetch, e.g. one a ticket linked to. 0 searches rather than fetches one. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: problem_id
parameters.description: The internal id of one problem to fetch, e.g. one a ticket linked to. 0 searches rather than fetches one. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: planned_after
parameters.description: Only include changes planned on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Narrows the search to changes, since problems carry no planned window. Defaults to empty, which applies no lower bound.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum causes to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0.

output.description: Changes and problems matching the request.

tools.name: FindRequester
tools.description:
Find a Freshservice requester by internal id, exact email, or name.

Exactly one of requester_id, email, or name must be given; supplying none
or more than one is rejected.

An email lookup matches character-for-character, so a guessed or
slightly-off address returns nothing even when the person is in the
directory. Retry by name when an email guess comes back empty.

parameters.name: requester_id
parameters.description: The internal requester id a ticket carries. 0 means no id lookup. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact email address of the requester to look up; an email that does not match a record character-for-character returns no results even if the person exists under a different address. Defaults to empty, meaning no email lookup.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A first or last name to search for among requesters, matched case-insensitively against each requester's full name. Every whitespace-separated word must appear somewhere in the name, in any order, so 'Ada Lovelace', 'Lovelace Ada', and 'Ada' all match the same person. Defaults to empty, meaning no name lookup.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum requesters to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: GetTicket
tools.description:
Read one ticket's whole story: fields, conversation, tasks, and any linked change or problem.

With every embed disabled this makes exactly one upstream request and sends
no include parameter at all; leaving any one embed enabled also resolves
the ticket's formal change and problem linkage.

Only a change or problem Freshservice itself formally linked to the ticket
is reported as linked. One merely named in the conversation text is not a
link, and has to be found by searching changes or problems for the affected
system's name instead.

The conversation returned is the most recent history rather than a
guaranteed-complete thread: a very long thread is reported as shortened, not
silently cut.

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: The Freshservice ticket's display number.

parameters.name: include_conversations
parameters.description: Include the most recent conversation/reply history. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: include_tasks
parameters.description: Include the ticket's tasks. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: include_requester
parameters.description: Include the requester's and department's names. Defaults to true.

output.description: The ticket, its people, its linkage, and its embedded collections.

tools.name: ListTickets
tools.description:
Narrow the Freshservice ticket queue to what is actionable.

NEW_AND_MINE lives on a predefined-view endpoint that rejects status and
priority filters, so combining them is rejected rather than silently
resolved; use ALL, UNASSIGNED, or BREACHING with a status/priority filter
instead. UNASSIGNED and BREACHING compose with status and priority.
BREACHING excludes tickets already resolved or closed unless a status is
explicitly given, since a past-due ticket that is already resolved or
closed no longer needs anyone's attention.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Which slice of the queue to return. ALL is every ticket, NEW_AND_MINE is the caller's own new and open tickets, UNASSIGNED has no assignee, BREACHING is past due and, unless status is also given, still open or pending (already resolved or closed tickets are excluded). Defaults to ALL.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only include tickets in this status: one of open, pending, resolved, closed, or a tenant-customized status's numeric code (visible in this tenant's Freshservice admin settings) for a status beyond those four defaults. Defaults to empty, which applies no status filter.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Only include tickets at this priority: one of low, medium, high, urgent, or a tenant-customized priority's numeric code for a value beyond those four defaults. Defaults to empty, which applies no priority filter.

parameters.name: requester_email
parameters.description: Only include tickets raised by this exact email address. Defaults to empty, which allows any requester.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only include tickets updated on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to empty, which applies no lower bound.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort field, only applied on the unfiltered ALL and NEW_AND_MINE views. Defaults to UPDATED_AT.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum tickets to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0.

output.description: Tickets in the requested slice of the queue.

tools.name: SearchServiceItems
tools.description:
Search the Freshservice service catalog for an item that covers an ask.

The catalog can be searched by term only and cannot be listed or browsed
in full under this grant: Freshservice gates the catalog's list and detail
endpoints behind a write scope this toolkit refuses to declare.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Free-text term to search the service catalog for. Required and must not be blank. The term is sent as typed to Freshservice's own catalog search, which matches it against item names and descriptions; how Freshservice combines several words is its rule, so a single specific word such as 'laptop' is the most reliable query, and a second call with another word beats one long phrase.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0.

output.description: Service catalog items matching the search term.

tools.name: SearchSolutions
tools.description:
Search the Freshservice knowledge base, or fetch one article in full by id.

Exactly one of search_term or article_id must be given; supplying both or
neither is rejected. Articles come back with their body text, not just a
title, so a single call is normally enough to answer the question.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Free-text term to search the knowledge base for. The term is sent as typed to Freshservice's own article search, which matches it against article titles and bodies; how Freshservice combines several words is its rule, so a single specific word or short phrase is the most reliable query. Defaults to empty; leave it empty when looking up a specific article by article_id.

parameters.name: article_id
parameters.description: The internal id of one article to fetch in full. 0 means no article lookup. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum articles to return (1-20). Defaults to 5.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0.

output.description: Solution articles matching the lookup, with their body text.

summary:
Freshservice is an IT service management platform by Freshworks. This toolkit lets LLM agents interact with Freshservice to triage tickets, search the knowledge base and service catalog, look up requesters, and correlate incidents with known causes.

## Capabilities

- **Ticket management**: Retrieve full ticket details (fields, conversation, tasks, linked changes/problems) and filter the ticket queue by actionable views, status, and priority.
- **Root cause correlation**: Search recent changes and tracked problems together in a single ranked call to explain a wave of related tickets.
- **Knowledge base access**: Search solution articles or fetch a full article by ID — body text included — in one call.
- **Service catalog search**: Find catalog items by search term (browsing the full catalog is blocked by scope constraints).
- **Requester lookup**: Resolve a Freshservice user by internal ID, exact email, or name.

## OAuth

Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Freshservice** provider. Arcade manages the OAuth flow; no manual token handling is required.

## Secrets

- **`FRESHSERVICE_SUBDOMAIN`**: Your Freshservice account subdomain — the prefix in your instance URL (e.g., `acme` from `acme.freshservice.com`). Find it by logging into your Freshservice instance and reading the subdomain from the browser address bar. This value identifies which Freshservice tenant API requests are routed to and is required for the toolkit to construct correct API endpoints.

Configure secrets in the Arcade dashboard or via the API: https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets — secrets can also be managed at https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets.
